 SKIP ADVERTISEMENT Trump Says He’s Open to Reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia Chief
 As he prepared for a visit to China, the president played down the fallout from Mr. Huang’s affair with a woman officials have identified as an intelligence asset for Beijing.
 Listen · 4:30 min Share full article 
 Jensen Huang earlier this year. On Monday, President Trump cast doubt on whether the woman with whom Mr. Huang had a relationship was actually a spy. Credit... Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times By Shawn McCreesh 
 Reporting from Washington
 Nov. 16, 2026 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. Encuentra más de nuestra cobertura en los resultados de búsqueda. Add The New York Times as a preferred source on Google Agrega The New York Times como fuente preferida en Google › 
 President Trump said on Monday that he was open to seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as the head of Nvidia, his latest public expression of support for the tech executive who resigned after admitting to an affair with a woman whom U.S. officials had identified as a Chinese intelligence asset.
 “I would not mind; I would not mind that,” Mr. Trump told reporters on the South Lawn of the White House as he departed for a trip to Asia, including a stop in China.
 “I think he learned a big lesson — I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another,” he added.
 The president’s remarks were his first in days on a scandal that has engulfed the chip-making giant at the heart of the artificial intelligence boom and raised questions about his handling of a potential national security threat. His backing of the former Nvidia chief added to a growing chorus from tech leaders who say Mr. Huang’s departure threatens to set the United States back in the A.I. race.
 The president cast doubt on whether Alice Huang , the woman with whom Mr. Huang had a relationship, was actually a spy.
 “I don’t know that she is a spy,” Mr. Trump said. “Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that’s a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she’s a spy. I don’t know that she was a spy at all.”
